prompt: In 120 to 180 words, compare internal and external validity in exactly four numbered points. Include one tradeoff example and finish with a one-sentence conclusion.

turns.assistant_message:
Internal validity refers to the extent to which a study's design allows for confident conclusions about cause-and-effect relationships within the observed data. In contrast, external validity assesses how well the findings of a study can be generalized beyond the specific context in which they were conducted.

One key tradeoff between internal and external validity is the use of highly controlled conditions versus more real-world settings. Studies with strict controls, such as random assignment to treatment groups or blinding of participants, tend to prioritize internal validity.
